Incorporating Beige Book insights alongside the March 17, 2021 FOMC statement and SLOOS: District reports indicate that vaccine progress was supporting firmer activity—consumer spending and auto sales strengthened, with a nascent pickup in travel and tourism. Employment was improving modestly, but labor demand varied by industry and skill, and firms faced acute shortages of qualified workers due to COVID-related labor constraints. Supply chain disruptions persisted. This corroborates the FOMC’s accommodative stance and cautious optimism while highlighting capacity constraints and lingering risks. Together with SLOOS (easier mortgage credit but still-cautious business lending), the balance of evidence tilts modestly positive, warranting a slight upward adjustment in sentiment.
